Segments with a material increase: ['Premium Thin & Light']

Focus segment: Premium Thin & Light. Premium Thin & Light has the highest recent battery complaint rate (6.9% [6.7%, 7.1%], E001). It is the only segment with a material increase from baseline: 4.4% to 6.9%, diff +2.5% (CI +2.2% to +2.8%), status intensified_long_standing (E005). This suggests battery complaints are a long-standing issue that has intensified, not a new one. Budget showed a small increase (+0.3%) but was labelled no_material_change (E002). Gaming (E003) and Mainstream (E004) show no material change. The complaint load is spread across 28 products, and the top product accounts for 12.6% of recent complaints (E005), so one product is unlikely to drive the pattern. This is descriptive only. The data have no distribution, availability or preference measures, so no causal conclusions can be drawn.

Declared H1 (complaint_comparison, less): Premium Thin & Light products positioned on battery life in their documents have a different post-first-sale battery complaint rate than other Premium Thin & Light products in the same cohort. This is an association only, and first sale is an estimate of market entry.

Declared H2 (launch_trajectory, two-sided): Premium Thin & Light products positioned on battery life have different sales per active model after their estimated first observed sale than the cohort of comparable products. This is descriptive and does not measure distribution or preference.

Alternative for P0113: High segment share may reflect a launch-size or distribution/availability effect, or a few-model segment composition artefact (share is relative to active models). The data contain no distribution or availability measure. Also, the first-month units (5,860) and early peak (21,541) are large, which fits a broad rollout rather than a battery-driven effect.

Alternative for P0113: The low battery complaint rate may reflect complaint-pool or comment-mix differences. P0113 has 4,826 comments against 1,465 for P0050, and other themes may dominate its comments, so battery would be a smaller share. Buyer mix could also differ, for example lighter-use buyers. Other causes include firmware or hardware differences. A high-volume product may attract more casual commenters. The cohort median of 9.0% is also well above the segment rate of 6.9%, which suggests a skewed cohort.

Alternative for P0113: The cohort is only 14 products with a wide spread in complaint rates (4.6% to 13.8%). The p-values come from several confirmatory tests, and the cohort definition (+/-6 months, ASP +/-30%) is a researcher choice. The result may be sensitive to those choices. Price is also a factor: ASP within 30% still allows differences in buyer expectations.

Alternative for P0050: The null result for P0050 may reflect low power: the complaint pool is small (1,465 comments, 129 complaints), the share test has only 14 comparators, and the p-values are far from significance. A null is not evidence of no effect. Price-and-volume months in 2024-M02 and 2024-M03 may also distort the share, though the sensitivity check suggests not.

Alternative for P0113: P0113 and P0050 share overlapping cohorts and first-sale months, and each appears in the other's cohort. P0113's very large share (18%) inflates the cohort comparison for P0050, since the cohort median is the same 3.88%. P0113 may also be an outlier that skews the others' comparisons.

Alternative for P0120: The first observed sale (2022-M04) coincides with a coverage-expansion month and the doc precedes it by 7 months. The product may have sold earlier, so the entry date is an artefact. This is consistent with the unreliable flag, and the product cannot be assessed.

Alternative for P0113: The segment-wide complaint rise from 4.4% to 6.9% may reflect complaint-pool changes (more comments, a shift in who comments, or greater attention to battery) and not worse batteries. The 28 products recently active against earlier ones also mean composition changed, so manufacturer responses cannot be tied to it.
